summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 131.31% YoY to INR 1,102.40 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.76%, while FY26 order book stood at 2.83 GW peak.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 execution of 2,727 MWp, with FY26 revenue of INR 3,331.42 crore (+108.51%) and PAT of INR 478.65 crore (+109.09%). Q4 benefited from a higher share of module-inclusive orders (about 50% of execution revenue), which lifted realisation to roughly INR 20 million per MW. Order inflow was flat-to-lower (about 2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW in FY25) and the order book fell from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW year on year. Management guided to a sustained EBITDA margin above 15%, with FY26 margin above 19.24%, and is self-funding a 54 MWp IPP fleet plus about 227 MWp under construction.

segments.name: EPC (incl. module-inclusive and BOS-only orders)
segments.commentary: FY26 execution of 2,727 MWp, the highest ever; Q4 realisation about INR 20 million/MW, with around 50% of Q4 execution revenue from module-inclusive orders. Management called the Q4 mix an aberration, citing a longer-run module-inclusive share of about 20% of MW.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M portfolio of 1.18 GWp, described as a recurring revenue base. No revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: 54 MWp operational, generating about INR 26 crore in FY26. About 227 MWp under construction, funded through internal accruals with no debt tied up; capex guided at INR 3-3.5 crore per MWp.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Early stage: one relatively small BESS project under execution, with management expecting the revenue stream to open in FY27. Inquiries are rising.

guidance_outlook: Order pipeline of about 36 GW (about 23 GW domestic, about 12 GW international); no hit ratio disclosed.
Current 2.8 GW order book expected to execute over the next 12-15 months, with new FY27 orders adding to it.
EBITDA margin: management says it aims to stay around 15% as a guiding threshold, while delivering above 19% in FY25 and FY26.
IPP capacity to be commissioned during FY27 from the CWIP-linked projects; no further IPP scale-up beyond the announced projects was quantified.
Management declined to give a firm FY27 execution number, saying it depends on order timing.
capex_capacity: 54 MWp IPP operational; about 227.1 MWp IPP under construction, funded internally.
Indicative solar capex of INR 3-3.5 crore per MWp, per management.
Management said the 227 MWp plus 54 MWp are the only capex for Waaree Renewable; group's INR 2,250 crore power infrastructure plan is separate and unclear in housing.
Unexecuted order book 2.83 GWp at year end; O&M portfolio 1.18 GWp.
demand_pricing: Realisation of about INR 1-1.25 crore per MW on the order book (management's rough range, caveated), with module-inclusive mix about 20% of MW long-run.
Order inflow around 2.3 GW in FY26 vs 2.4 GW in FY25; management attributed the book decline to bilateral negotiations on large orders, not competition.
Geographic exposure: Rajasthan is the heaviest, with Gujarat, MP, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra also contributing.
Management said all contracts are fixed-price, but module cost increases are passed through to customers in module-inclusive turnkey orders.
Receivables mostly under 6 months, many secured by letters of credit; no material government payment stretch as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 realisation about INR 20 million/MW, and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around 50% of Q4 execution revenue came from module-inclusive orders, so the spike reflects project mix rather than a new pricing trend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW, and what is the inflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 inflow was about 2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW in FY25, with negotiations taking longer on large orders; about 36 GW of pipeline is under bilateral discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins sustainable at 19-20% vs the historical 25% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly margin depends on the customer order mix, FY26 EBITDA margin exceeded 19.24%, and 15% is a guiding threshold rather than a calculated floor.

qa_highlights.question: Does the CTUIL substation clarity issue in Rajasthan threaten new EPC awards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC contracts are awarded only after developers complete connectivity and land studies, so existing backlog is not affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding and IRR of the IPP strategy, and what is the 227 MWp capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IPP is funded entirely from internal accruals with no debt, and indicative capex is INR 3-3.5 crore per MWp; IRR was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is BESS cost per MW and is there any data centre revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give BESS cost per MW, citing project-specific scope; it said there is no firm data centre order yet and only one small BESS project is in execution.

risks_watch: Order inflow has been flat to lower (2.3 GW in FY26 vs 2.4 GW in FY25) and the order book fell from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW.
Q4 margin of 18.76% is below the 25% level some analysts cited for Q4 in prior years; management's 15% guidance is a threshold, not a forecast.
Receivables rose sharply year on year (about double), with management attributing most to late-quarter billing and LCs; watch the collection cycle and inventory build.
Substation clarity in Rajasthan (about 60 GW awaiting coordinates per CTUIL) could affect developer award timing.
Hit ratio on the 36 GW pipeline was not disclosed; the FY27 execution number was not guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and the pipeline, but evasive on specifics: management declined to quantify BESS cost, data centre opportunities, IPP IRR, pipeline hit ratio and module pricing. Management repeatedly tied quarterly variation to order mix and said it avoids tenders that do not meet its margin and risk-reward thresholds.
key_quotes: So whatever orders we are executing, more or less, we are getting the similar kind of order in the current financial year.
But always we are mentioning that the EBITDA margin should remain around 15%, but definitely we are delivering on a continuous basis.
So, as far as Waaree Renewable Technologies is concerned, the pricing of varying this module price will not impact everything.

adds.what: 227.1 MWp IPP under construction, funded internally (capex INR 3-3.5 crore/MWp)

growth.why: No firm FY27 execution number given; 2.83 GW order book to execute over 12-15 months with order inflow down ~5% to 2.3 GW, and IPP additions of 227 MWp under construction (self-funded) are only partly tied to commissioning timing, so outlook is flat to modestly positive.
